notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. result.json gives head e83b4f2 with uncommitted changes; the skill copy the runs read (scratchpad/check5/skill) is identical to the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, which differs from e83b4f2 only by the do: rule in SKILL.md.

git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md (the one-step with rule, the do: rule, the captures rule) and testing.md (Assert with patterns). macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of <previous>/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json and the check-2 grade file: a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, validation in the macro body outside quote does not; a one-line three-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens.

Changed rule, graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Its last three sentences changed since check-2, and the verdicts now turn on "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." Violating runs out of four, per sentence. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head: an accessor, a predicate, or a short pattern-matching clause.": 0 of 4 (no do: on a body of more than one expression). "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 4. "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": blank-line part 0 of 4; keep-on-do: part 2 of 4 as a judgement call (sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 write validate_handler!/1's :ok clause as a block, although only the raise clause needs one and its do: form would be a guard-wrapped head, which the rule now accepts); this does not decide either verdict. "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": 2 of 4 (sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, validate_path!/1: one do: clause and two raise clauses that would wrap under do:). "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper; a head that `mix format` wraps because of a long guard is fine as wrapped.": 0 of 4 (every one-expression body that would wrap under do: was written as a block; checked with Code.format_string!). Any sentence: 2 of 4 (sonnet-1, sonnet-2); both haiku runs clean. At check-2 all four runs violated this rule.

match_segments/3 per run. All four write it as four clauses: two short do: clauses (the [], [] base case and the catch-all :error) and two recursive block clauses, each block set apart by blank lines. Each block clause's body is one expression too long for its head (117 to 155 characters as a do: line), so two of four clauses need blocks. Two of four is not most, so the mixed form is clean under the current text in all four: haiku-1 lines 92-102, haiku-2 lines 116-126, sonnet-1 lines 148-158, sonnet-2 lines 130-140. At check-2 the same shape was the violation in haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 under the old several-blocks wording.

Wrapped do: lines per run: none in any of the four files. haiku-1 and haiku-2 put every long one-expression body in a block (haiku-1 module_name?/1; haiku-2 __put_route__/3, module_name?/1, compile_error!/2). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 avoided the guard wrap that was their check-2 violation by writing validate_handler!/1's :ok clause as a do ... end block (sonnet-1 lines 127-129, sonnet-2 lines 112-114); under the current text the wrapped do: form would have been fine, so the block is the judgement call noted above.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects (one per run, the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file, with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex, except for sonnet-2, whose file defines its own stubs). haiku-1 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:call, 2}) and sonnet-1 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1}) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). haiku-2 expands with Macro.expand and reports (compile). sonnet-2 does not expand the handler at all and passes the alias into __define__/3, which runs in the router's module body, and reports (compile); a variant with its stub modules moved to lib/handlers.ex also reports (compile), so the stubs are not the cause.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's file loaded, then one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module" compiled with Code.compile_string. All eight fail while the router compiles: haiku-2 with CompileError raised while get expands; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from __define__/3, which get's quote calls. Messages omit the nofile:3: location prefix.

Format: sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 pass mix format --check-formatted (both wrote get("/", MyApp.PageHandler)). haiku-1 (lines 108-109) and haiku-2 (lines 132-133) fail it only because they wrote get "/", MyApp.PageHandler without parentheses, which result.json records as format_ok false. All four compile without warnings with elixir and with mix compile.
Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md with Read calls before writing the file, each reference twice, matching result.json reads and satisfying the Expected reads line.

Against check-2: haiku-1 moved from a direct attribute write and Macro.expand to __define__/3 with Macro.expand_literals and is now clean on all eight rules; haiku-2 moved from a direct attribute write to __put_route__/3 but still uses Macro.expand; sonnet-1 is unchanged on the seven macro and library rules; sonnet-2 dropped Macro.expand_literals and now makes handlers compile-time dependencies.

Smoke test outside the rules: all four return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope"; haiku-2 returns atom param keys (%{id: "42"}), the others string keys (%{"id" => "42"}).
